method: Sequential matched baseline and candidate. Three fresh implicit wallets per arm. Same custody versions. One SDK and harness serve both arms. Only the Gateway identity query differs. Only the NEAR signer is loaded. First signature is an independently verified NEP-413 message without account funding.
scope: Existing staging testnet resources. No new infrastructure or package release.
changes: Read the registration authentication method and its authority in one tenant-scoped SQL query.
Remove the subsequent duplicate authority read from session issuance and mixed registration continuation.
Keep active-state, credential, wallet, canonical digest, replay and session checks.

outcome: No finalization speedup established. Candidate finalization median increased by 293ms. Overall registration-to-verified-message median decreased while unchanged Yao code also ran faster. Retain the coherent identity query without attributing the overall decrease to it.
limitations: Three sequential samples per arm establish neither percentiles nor a maximum guarantee.
Authenticated Yao and wallet-commit metrics sum corresponding HTTP durations per sample, never stage medians.
Browser registration-to-signature time includes automation and UI settlement. Fresh wallets do not prove cold Workers or DOs.
Gateway-wide D1 and backend Console call counts remain unknown. Application timers omit some CPU work.
Existing APAC home hints remain. Actual physical colocation was not remeasured.
